headline: Wattimena v Doets: 13th meeting with £60,000 guaranteed
standfirst: Jermaine Wattimena and Kevin Doets, split 7 wins to 6 in their meetings, play for a Grand Slam semi-final tonight; Gerwyn Price meets Niko Springer afterwards.
body: The best tie on tonight's Grand Slam of Darts quarter-final card is the one between two players who know each other well. Jermaine Wattimena and Kevin Doets have met 13 times, with Doets ahead by seven wins to six, and the winner of the first-to-16 match at 7:15pm is guaranteed £60,000. The loser takes home £35,000.

Wattimena arrives as the story of the week after knocking out Luke Littler 10-8 in the last 16. The world No 18 has a 12-month average of 94.71 and has won 92 of 149 matches in that time. He has been this far before: his best Grand Slam finish is a quarter-final, in 2024.

Doets, ranked 23rd, is the stronger scorer on paper. His 12-month average is 96.44 and he has won 127 of 180 matches, a higher share than Wattimena's. He is making his first appearance on record at the event, and beat Cameron Menzies 10-5 in the last 16 after group-stage wins over Josh Rock and Tommy Morris.

The second quarter-final follows at 8:45pm and looks less even on the numbers. Gerwyn Price, the world No 4, won this event in 2018 and averages 98.67 over the last 12 months, with four titles in that time. He beat Ryan Searle 10-7 in the last 16.

Niko Springer, ranked 34th, averages 91.85 and has not won a title in the past year. He has still knocked out Rob Cross 10-8 to match his last-16 finish from 2025, and has met Price once before, losing.
